At the same time the Finance Committee was meeting here on December 13th, there was also a Town Council meeting that occurred. And at that Town Council meeting, it was scheduled to be a public hearing for those two projects.
During the meeting, the Town Council decided to cancel the public hearing, and they decided to remand the applications back to the Planning Commission.

And the explanation that was provided at the meeting was that the updates that the county had provided the town council at their request at their November 30th meeting were never viewed by the Planning Commission because they made the recommendation back in October and they felt that it should go back to the Planning Commission since they did not see the updated plan.
So as a result of that, we went to the next Planning Commission meeting, which occurred on January the 5th last week, and the updated concept plans were presented to the Planning Commission.

They have not made any recommendations yet. They have not voted on their recommendations for that application. There is a meeting scheduled for Thursday for additional discussion on those applications.

And their goal is to have a recommendation to the town council by December 19th. Sorry, January 19th. During the discussion that took place last week, like I said, there was no recommendations made, But there were several comments that were kind of themes that we heard.

One is they did appreciate the revisions we made to the concept plans, meaning that we did hear them and we were trying to address their concerns. But at the same time, they still expressed concern about the scale of the projects.
They still felt they were too large for the rural character of Percival. And they also were just concerned that it didn't meet or it didn't provide the benefit to the citizens of Percival.

Specifically, their concerns had to do with they still feel the park and ride lot is too large and they feel that the proposed athletic field lighting, the hours are too long and they would like to have that cut back.

and some even suggested have no lights at all. So those are still going to be issues. And, again, we don't know how they're going to ultimately recommend, but it's both our opinion and Parks and Rec opinion that there's a very good chance that the athletic field lighting will not be what we would generally need for a Loudoun County Parks and Rec facility.

And we'll see how that plays out. Moving on to, and let me move on to the questions they had on the park and ride facility. They expressed a concern about the size of the park and ride facility, which is proposed to have approximately 250 spaces.
Some of the town council members did, sorry, some of the planning commissioners did note that they're not seeing park and ride usage of that volume post-COVID. And that is accurate.
We did note in the item that currently for the existing Percival Park and Ride as well as the Harmony Park and Ride lots, right now the combined usage of those is less than 100 vehicles right now.
Now, in the future, it is expected that that demand will increase, but the timing associated with that is not easy to predict, given we're in a sort of unprecedented time right now.

So those are the issues that we heard regarding the park and ride as well as the Fields Farm Park. Moving to the 7690 interchange project, the town council also discussed that specific project at their December 13th meeting.

Even though the actual design plans are approved, we are in the process of trying to get a plat approved for some construction easements, as well as to obtain some right-of-way for one of the ramps associated with the interchange.

As part of that particular application, there is also a need to vacate an existing floodplain easement because that existing easement will ultimately be in the ramp lane. So as part of our obligation under VDOT procedures, we need to clear the right-of-way so that we can then get authorization to perform construction for the project.

So that is what the particular issue is with 7690. It is not actually getting the plans approved. It is getting a plat approved. So the issues that are noted in the item associated with that particular project is, one, these projects are all interrelated.

So impact to the 7690 project, if it were delayed or there be an extensive delay, that affects access to the Western Loudoun Park and Ride, which makes it much less effective, as well as it impacts traffic operations at the Route 7, 287 interchange, which is another smart scale project.

So what is mentioned in the issues section of the item is that, one, the issues that the town is bringing up regarding the floodplain adjacent to the 7690 interchange is independent of the actual project.

As mentioned previously, the project plans have all been approved, and we're just attempting to get a PLAT approved. And through that review process, it was realized by the town that the floodplain in that area is still under old, it's mapped using old data that dates back to the 70s.

And that for the section of the project that is within the county's limits, we, as required by the county FSM, did an updated floodplain study. And as part of that study, we utilized newer methodology and the mapping of that floodplain, the existing condition floodplain pre-construction expanded because conditions have changed.

The town then asked us to take a look at what would happen in the town. And indeed, the floodplain modeled would be expanded beyond what is currently mapped from the late 70s information. In our floodplain alteration studies, we have documented that the project itself does not create any rise in the floodplain.

This is just an existing condition that's based on new information and new conditions. So that is what is really causing a lot of this concern, and it really is independent of the project. The last thing I just want to note is I mentioned how any effects on the 7-690 project also could potentially impact the 7-287 project.
So if, for whatever reason, the 7-690 project were to be extensively delayed, the traffic operations at the 7-287 interchange would be impacted.

And what our consultant modeled, at least using some preliminary data, is that opening date, the 7287 interchange would still work, but somewhere in the 2030s, it would start to fail and not meet the level of service requirements.
And the way the project is currently scoped, our design year is 2044, and that interchange would not operate at an acceptable level in 2044 if the 7690 interchange is not in operation.

So that's sort of a summary of what has occurred and what are the impacts, and we're open to any questions you might have. Great. Thank you so much. Supervisor Briskman? Thank you. Thank you for that update.
